qualification: Intel Linux guest block enumeration and host-backed read
observations: Generated ACPI advertises distinct console and block MMIO devices with separate GSIs. ACPICA disassembly and recompilation passed before the Intel run.
Linux opened /dev/vda, verified BLKGETSIZE64 equals 33554432, sought to 4096 and read 4096 bytes matching a distinct guest marker and all remaining zero padding.
The VMM required a host-backed attachment, DRIVER_OK and a guest queue response before accepting the ring3 userspace result. The preboot read does not increment that response counter.

The first Intel attempt failed during Linux device configuration at GPA 0xf000111a. Adding operand-size-prefixed 16-bit MOV support resolved the failure. Host tests cover word loads, stores, immediate stores, truncation and preservation of upper register bits.
The successful Intel run also passed the preboot block read and bidirectional console exchange. No qualification QEMU remained afterward.
limitations: The disk is a fresh read-only fixture. Writable flush/reboot persistence and pinned Debian acceptance remain unqualified.
This run does not establish multi-client Intel isolation or resource reclamation.
Canonical integration, GUI qualification and the v0.4 release remain incomplete.
